app.title: FSC Error Bar Calculator
app.summary: A person picks one of three ways to estimate error bars, sets the confidence width (sigma) and, for bootstrapping, the number of resamples. They upload two half-maps and press Run. The app checks that both volumes are 3D and the same shape, then computes the correlation in each frequency shell along with lower and upper confidence bounds. It plots the curve and its bounds against a 0.143 threshold line, shows the values in a table and offers them as a CSV download.

task.text: Compute the Fourier shell correlation between two independent half-maps, with a confidence interval in every shell, so the resolution estimate comes with its uncertainty.

data.text: Two independently reconstructed 3D density volumes of the same size, in MRC format. They are turned into a table of correlation values, one row per spatial-frequency shell, with lower and upper bounds.
data.item: a spherical shell of Fourier-space voxels at one spatial frequency, compared between the two half-maps

stage.text: estimating and checking map resolution after 3D reconstruction, before reporting the structure

mechanism.text: A single-page form gathers the error method, sigma, bootstrap count and the two half-map files. Pressing Run computes the curve and its bounds, which appear as a line chart with a 0.143 threshold line, a table of the same values and a CSV download.

field.text: Fourier shell correlation resolution estimation in cryo-electron microscopy

workflow.name: compute a curve with confidence bounds from two replicate measurements and export it

steps.step: choose how the uncertainty is estimated
steps.here: A dropdown picks Fisher Z-transform, Bootstrap or Analytical Variance. A number input sets sigma, and the bootstrap sample count appears only when Bootstrap is chosen.
Two file uploaders take the half map 1 and half map 2 .mrc files, and pressing Run reads them along with the voxel size.
The run stops with an error if the two volumes differ in shape or are not 3D.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Both volumes are Fourier transformed. For each spherical shell the app computes the correlation between the maps and its lower and upper bounds from voxel count and sigma (or bootstrap percentiles). It also converts the shell index into spatial frequency in 1/Å.

steps.step: look over the result at a glance
steps.here: A line chart shows the FSC curve with dashed upper and lower limits and a gray FSC = 0.143 line. The x-axis is labelled in 1/Å.
A table lists frequency, FSC and both limits for each shell, and a button downloads it as a CSV file.

distinctive: The comparison is between two independent half-reconstructions, and their agreement in each frequency shell is the measure of resolution.
Three interchangeable ways to compute the uncertainty (analytic transform, resampling, closed-form variance) can be run on the same data.
The width of each shell's interval depends on how many voxels the shell has, so the bounds are wide at low frequency and narrow further out.
A fixed 0.143 correlation threshold line marks the conventional resolution cutoff on the plot.
